name: LA-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a PVI of R+20
Steve Scalise is a well-funded, senior incumbent
Democrat Lauren Jewett has raised only about $143k with little cash on hand
Prediction markets price Republican win chances around 96%
model.rationale: Scalise holds a seat that leans Republican by twenty points, has out-raised his challenger by roughly 75-to-1, and markets give him about a 96% chance of winning. Nothing in the available evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected incumbent retirement could open the door, but no such signs appear in the current evidence.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Louisiana's 1st District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of about twenty points toward the GOP. Steve Scalise, the House Majority Leader, is seeking reelection with the advantages of seniority, name recognition, and a large financial edge. He has raised more than $10.6 million and holds nearly $3.9 million in cash.

Democratic challenger Lauren Jewett has raised about $143,000 and had under $12,000 on hand, leaving her little capacity to compete in this conservative district. Prediction markets give Scalise roughly a 96% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. The seat is expected to remain safely in Republican hands.
